area: Android Guaranteed-Alarm Architecture (OS-level backstop decoupled from the tracking loop)
current_gap: The audible wake-up exists ONLY inside the Flutter background isolate. `AlarmController.checkAndTriggerAlarm` (lib/services/tracking/alarm_controller.dart:298) is the sole path that fires the alarm, and it is driven per-GPS-tick from `_checkAndTriggerAlarm` (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:2171, :2440). The actual sound comes from Dart `AlarmPlayer.playSelected()` inside `NotificationService.showWakeUpAlarm` (lib/services/notification_service.dart:794-826), and the alarm notification channel is deliberately silent (`playSound:false`, notification_service.dart:617/728). So if the isolate is dead — Doze/App Standby, OEM kill (Xiaomi/Oppo/Vivo/Samsung on the India-first market), heartbeat_monitor pausing tracking on UI death, or OOM — there is NOTHING scheduled at the OS level to make noise. AlarmReceiver.kt is a 1-line empty file, there is no AlarmManager usage anywhere, no BOOT_COMPLETED receiver, no exact-alarm permission in AndroidManifest.xml, and the manifest declares USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT but no code ever schedules an OS alarm to post that FSI. A sleeping rider whose process died mid-journey is never woken = product death.
recommended_design:
Belt-and-suspenders with THREE independent layers, where the guarantee lives in a layer that does NOT depend on the Flutter process being alive.

LAYER 1 — SUSPENDERS (accurate, already exists): the live tracking loop / EKF continues to fire the precise alarm via AlarmController when the isolate is alive. Unchanged.

LAYER 2 — BELT (the guarantee): an OS-scheduled AlarmManager exact alarm, decoupled from the tracking service, that fires a native full-screen-intent alarm even if the app process is dead. Schedule with `AlarmManager.setAlarmClock(AlarmClockInfo(triggerAtEpoch, showPI), operationPI)` — it is the most Doze-resistant call (system leaves low-power mode to deliver it, delivery time is never adjusted [HARD FACT, developer.android.com alarms doc]) and, being an alarm-clock, is effectively exempt from the SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM gating [INFERENCE from AOSP AlarmManagerService; mitigate by ALSO declaring USE_EXACT_ALARM which WakePoint legitimately qualifies for as an alarm app under Play policy]. The PendingIntent targets a NEW, real `AlarmReceiver.kt` (BroadcastReceiver). The receiver does NOT touch Dart: it posts a notification on a NEW dedicated channel `geowake_backstop_alarm` whose SOUND IS BAKED INTO THE CHANNEL (alarm ringtone URI + AudioAttributes USAGE_ALARM + IMPORTANCE_HIGH), with `setCategory(CATEGORY_ALARM)`, `setFullScreenIntent(mainActivityPI, true)`, ongoing+insistent. Because the sound is OS-driven (channel), no live process or AlarmPlayer is needed to make noise. FSI launches MainActivity, which already has `showWhenLocked=true` + `turnScreenOn=true` (AndroidManifest.xml:31-32) so the screen wakes over the keyguard. [HARD FACT: when USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT is granted the full activity launches regardless of lock state; when denied it degrades to a 60s heads-up HUN — still audible via the channel sound — so the audible wake survives even a denied FSI, source.android.com/docs/core/permissions/fsi-limits.]

LAYER 3 — RESCHEDULE + PERSISTENCE: recompute the backstop instant every tick as ETA changes, and persist the absolute target epoch so a BOOT_COMPLETED receiver re-arms it after reboot.

Backstop instant = arrivalEpoch − thresholdLead − safetyLead, where arrivalEpoch = now + smoothedETA_to_destination (falls to API/metro-scheduled ETA before EKF converges), thresholdLead converts the user's alarm (N min / N km→time / stops→time) into lead time, and safetyLead ≈ 60–90 s of deliberate EARLINESS (being early is harmless, late = death). A HARD-FLOOR backstop is armed at t0 from the journey's API/scheduled ETA so an alarm is scheduled even if the isolate dies in the first seconds before any good ETA exists. When Layer 1 fires the real alarm it cancels the pending backstop; if the backstop fires first (process was dead), it is self-sufficient. Recompute is cheap: only re-arm when the new instant differs from the armed instant by > ~20 s to avoid alarm churn.

Keep USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT (already line 13). Optionally also add SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM for max-target flexibility, but USE_EXACT_ALARM is sufficient and cannot be revoked by the user.

MANIFEST: register the two receivers inside <application>: <receiver android:name=".AlarmReceiver" android:exported="false"/> and <receiver android:name=".BootReceiver" android:exported="true"><intent-filter><action android:name="android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED"/><action android:name="android.intent.action.MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED"/></intent-filter></receiver>.

This channel MUST make sound on its own (unlike the existing silent geowake_alarm_channel_v4) because the backstop runs with no Dart process.

IMPLEMENT AlarmReceiver.kt (replace the empty 1-line file at android/app/src/main/java/com/example/geowake2/AlarmReceiver.kt): onReceive builds a Notification on `geowake_backstop_alarm` with setCategory(CATEGORY_ALARM), setFullScreenIntent(PendingIntent to MainActivity with FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK, true), setOngoing(true), extras carrying the title/body/stop-name passed in the Intent, then NotificationManager.notify(BACKSTOP_ID). Read the alarm-fired flag from a plain file/SharedPreferences and no-op if Layer 1 already fired. Acquire a short WakeLock (1–2s) only to cover the post() window.

CREATE BootReceiver.kt: on BOOT_COMPLETED / MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED, read the persisted backstop epoch (written by Layer 3) from SharedPreferences; if it is in the future and the session is still active, re-arm the AlarmManager alarm. CREATE a MethodChannel `geowake/backstop` in MainActivity.kt exposing schedule(epochMillis,title,body) and cancel(): schedule calls alarmManager.setAlarmClock(AlarmClockInfo(epochMillis, showPI), PendingIntent.getBroadcast(...AlarmReceiver...FLAG_UPDATE_CURRENT|FLAG_IMMUTABLE)); cancel calls alarmManager.cancel(pi) + notificationManager.cancel(BACKSTOP_ID). WIRE RECOMPUTE (lib/services/trackingservice.dart): in the location tick right after `_smoothedETA = _locationStreamHandler.smoothedETA;` (line 2113) and before/after `_checkAndTriggerAlarm` (line 2171 and the injected path line 2440), compute backstopEpoch = now + (etaToDestination - thresholdLeadSeconds - safetyLeadSeconds), and if |backstopEpoch - lastArmedEpoch| > 20s call BackstopAlarm.schedule(...). ARM HARD-FLOOR AT START: in startTracking (lib/services/trackingservice.dart:228) once the initial API/scheduled ETA is known, immediately schedule a first backstop so an OS alarm exists from t0 even if the isolate dies within seconds.

CANCEL ON FIRE + ON END: in AlarmController.triggerAlarmNotification (alarm_controller.dart:251) after a FINAL destination alarm, call BackstopAlarm.cancel() so the belt does not double-fire. Also surface a battery-optimization exemption request (ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS) here — the single highest-leverage OEM-survival lever, currently absent.

> **Naming note:** There is no "iOS 19." Apple renamed the 2025 release to **iOS 26** (shipped Sept 2025); iOS 27 was announced at WWDC June 2026. The "iOS 18/19 era" = iOS 18 (2024) + iOS 26 (2025+). CoreLocation fundamentals below are unchanged since iOS 16.4.

### The one-paragraph truth
On iOS you **cannot** do what WakePoint does on Android — keep the IMU/EKF dead-reckoning alive through a deep tunnel while suspended. iOS grants **no background mode for raw CoreMotion/accelerometer** (HARD FACT). The whole iOS design must therefore pivot to a **system-scheduled, time-based alarm** that fires independent of the app process. iOS 26's **AlarmKit** makes this viable and is the single most important 2026 development for this product.

### Current code state (verified)
| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| No `UIBackgroundModes` at all | `ios/Runner/Info.plist` lines 4–60 — key absent |
| Background location never enabled | All 3 call-sites use plain `LocationSettings`, never `AppleSettings`: `maptracking.dart:616`, `gps_position_provider.dart:28`, `location_manager.dart:45` |
| No native alarm/audio bridge | `AppDelegate.swift` is bare (13 lines); no AVAudioSession, no AlarmKit |
| Always-usage string present | `Info.plist:52` — good, but unused without background mode |

**1. Continuous background location — stays alive *while signal flows*.**
`allowsBackgroundLocationUpdates=true` + `pausesLocationUpdatesAutomatically=false` + `UIBackgroundModes:location` keeps the app **running** (not just un-terminated) as long as location events arrive. Since iOS 16.4, this needs `distanceFilter=kCLDistanceFilterNone` and accuracy ≥ hundredMeters, and it must be armed before backgrounding ([Apple docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corelocation/handling-location-updates-in-the-background), [iOS 16.4 changes](https://cropsly.com/blog/location-updates-changes-in-ios-16-4)). **HARD FACT:** location background mode prevents *termination*, not *suspension* — when updates stop (tunnel), the app is suspended ([Apple forum 69152](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/69152)).

**2. The tunnel kills the EKF (un-closable).** When GPS + cell both vanish, updates stop → app suspends → **CoreMotion stops delivering** → EKF freezes. iOS explicitly does not allow background raw-IMU ([Apple forum 61870](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/61870), [Mysk](https://mysk.blog/2021/10/24/accelerometer-ios/)). There is no wakelock equivalent. **Live inertial dead-reckoning through a deep tunnel is not achievable on iOS.**

**3. Background AUDIO keep-alive — works technically, but don't.** A silent looping `.playback` session *would* hold the process (and CoreMotion) alive through a tunnel. 4. **Time-Sensitive notification** at ETA — fallback for iOS < 26.
5. **AVAudioSession `.playback`** — only for in-app alarming, not keep-alive.

- Non-wake-up sensors (which `SensorManager.registerListener`, and thus sensors_plus, uses by default): *"It is the responsibility of applications to keep a partial wake lock should they wish to receive events from non-wake-up sensors while the screen is off."* Without a wakelock, events buffer in the hardware FIFO and are delivered only on wake; *"in the extreme case where the FIFO is nonexistent, all events generated while the SoC is in suspend mode are lost."* — [AOSP suspend-mode](https://source.android.com/docs/core/interaction/sensors/suspend-mode)

- CoreMotion has **no background mode of its own**: *"there is no Core Motion UIBackgroundModes setting… you might run in the background because you're using Core Location, and take advantage of this to employ Core Motion as well."* — [apeth.com ch.35](https://www.apeth.com/iOSBook/ch35.html), [Core Motion](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coremotion/)

- `CMSensorRecorder` is **not** a real-time rescue: it records **accelerometer only (no gyro), at ~50 Hz, into a retrospective batched ring buffer you read after the fact** — you cannot feed a live 6-DOF EKF or wake anyone in real time from it. Useful only for post-hoc analysis.

Instrument `startFusion()` in `lib/services/sensor_fusion.dart`: count every accel and gyro event, and every ~10 s of wall-clock (checked inside the accel callback) append one line to a log file via the existing `ekf_logger`: `{wallClockISO, accelCount, gyroCount}`. Then:

2. Effective Hz per bucket = count / elapsed. Expect **~500 accel/10 s (50 Hz)** after the fix vs **~50 (5 Hz)** today. **Zero buckets = FGS was killed or CPU suspended.**
3. Run on a **Pixel/Samsung AND a Redmi/Realme** (India-representative), each with battery-opt exemption **ON and OFF**.

This one ride tells you the *real* background rate and gap pattern — which is the only honest basis for deciding whether the EKF is production-usable.

### 6. Fallback if background IMU is not reliable
Make DR an **accuracy enhancer over a GPS + route-schedule + barometer alarm floor**, never the sole wake mechanism. Wire `onGpsUnavailable` (currently never called in production) to explicitly enter a degraded mode that fires on **last-known-GPS + elapsed-time-to-stop + barometer altitude cues** (sensors_plus exposes `BarometerEvent` on Android and iOS/CMAltimeter). ## Area: Process-death & Boot Recovery + State Persistence

**Verdict: SHOWSTOPPER.** The brief's death scenario — board, sleep, reboot/kill, no wake — is currently reproducible on any Android 14+ device and on any device whose tracking isolate dies, because **every alarm depends on the live GPS/EKF isolate and there is no time-based backstop.**

### What I verified in the code (HARD FACT)

**The plugin already ships most of the recovery scaffolding, and it is wired.** `flutter_background_service_android` 6.3.1 merges into your APK a `BootReceiver`, a `WatchdogReceiver`, and `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED` / `WAKE_LOCK` / `stopWithTask="false"` (plugin `AndroidManifest.xml`). Concretely:
- `BackgroundService.onStartCommand` returns **`START_NOT_STICKY`** (`BackgroundService.java:184`) — so the OS does **not** sticky-restart. Restart is instead driven by `WatchdogReceiver`, which re-arms an `AlarmManager` alarm every 5 s (and 1 s on `onTaskRemoved`) and respawns the service when `!isManuallyStopped && !isRunning` (`WatchdogReceiver.java`).
- `BootReceiver` starts the service on boot **only if** `Config.isAutoStartOnBoot()` (SharedPref `auto_start_on_boot`) is true (`BootReceiver.java`). `AndroidConfiguration.autoStartOnBoot` **defaults `true`** (`configs.dart:73`) and WakePoint's `configure()` (`trackingservice.dart:209`) does not override it, and `initializeService()` runs on every launch from `splash_screen.dart:73`. **So the boot receiver is armed.**
- The plugin **does** hold a `PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK` while the service runs (`BackgroundService.getLock().acquire()`, `BackgroundService.java:198`). The brief's "NO wakelock anywhere" is true for *app* code but not at the plugin layer during an active service.
- `_onStart` already has a recovery branch for `initialData == null` (`trackingservice.dart:2020-2102`) that reloads the snapshot and re-registers the route. This is the path both watchdog-respawn and boot-restart take.

**So why does recovery still fail?** Three gaps, each independently fatal:

1. **Android 14 (targetSdk 34) forbids starting a `location`-typed foreground service from the background, including from `BOOT_COMPLETED`** — the system throws `SecurityException` because the app lacks while-in-use at that moment ([restrictions-bg-start](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/fgs/restrictions-bg-start), [fgs-types-required](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/14/changes/fgs-types-required)). Your merged service is typed `location|mediaPlayback`. So the plugin's boot/watchdog restart of that service **throws and dies on exactly the phones the brief targets.** (HARD FACT for the restriction; INFERENCE that it throws in your specific config — worth a device test on A14/15.)
2. **No wake is independent of the GPS loop.** All firing happens in `alarm_controller.dart` inside the service isolate. Kill the isolate (or fail to restart it per #1) and nothing fires. Even a *successful* boot restart re-enters GPS cold — underground/at speed the rider can pass the stop before a fix.
3. **`AlarmReceiver.kt` is empty (0 bytes)** and there is no exact-alarm at all. The snapshot (`tracking_state_store.dart`) persists `ekfS`/`ekfSigmaS` fragments but **no absolute predicted-arrival timestamp**, and `AlarmController` fired-state (`_destinationAlarmFiredByKey`, `_firedLegIds`) is **in-memory only** — lost on every restart.

### The fix: an exact-alarm backstop that does not need the tracking loop

The guarantee must not be a running isolate; it must be a scheduled OS alarm. `AlarmManager.setAlarmClock()` is **Doze-exempt and the system exits Doze shortly before it fires** ([Schedule alarms](https://developer.android.com/develop/background-work/services/alarms)) — the strongest wake primitive Android offers. Design:

- The tracking loop keeps refining ETA and, on every recompute, calls a native `ExactAlarmScheduler.schedule(predictedArrivalEpochMs)` (via MethodChannel `geowake/exact_alarm`, mirrored on the existing `geowake/alarm_haptics` channel in `MainActivity`). It persists `predictedArrivalEpochMs` into the snapshot.
- The alarm's `PendingIntent` targets a **now-populated `AlarmReceiver.kt`** that raises the wake via a **full-screen-intent, IMPORTANCE_HIGH notification on `geowake_alarm_channel_v3`** (both the channel and `USE_FULL_SCREEN_INTENT` already exist) plus sound/vibration — **without starting the location FGS**, so it is legal from a cold receiver on Android 14+.
- Live GPS/EKF only ever fires *earlier* than the backstop. If the loop is alive it wakes the rider precisely; if the loop is dead, the last-scheduled backstop still fires at predicted arrival. This is the core inversion.

For **reboot**, add an **app-owned `WakeBootReceiver`** whose primary job is to **re-arm the backstop from the snapshot** (not to restart the location FGS, which is illegal from boot on A14+). Permissions: `USE_EXACT_ALARM` (Android 13+, grantable **without** a user prompt for alarm-clock-category apps — appropriate and Play-policy-allowed for a wake-up alarm; [schedule-exact-alarms](https://developer.android.com/about/versions/14/changes/schedule-exact-alarms)) plus `SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM` for Android 12.

For **process death**, keep the plugin watchdog (make `autoStartOnBoot: true` explicit and call `setAutoStartOnBootMode(true)` at journey start), and add a **15-min WorkManager health-worker** as a secondary reviver (WorkManager reschedules itself across reboot). Both are defense-in-depth; the backstop is the guarantee. Persist `AlarmController` fired-state + a `schemaVersion` so restart neither re-fires a fired leg nor loses the destination latch.

### Restore sequence (target state)

Boot or respawn → receiver/`_onStart` reads `tracking_active_v1` + snapshot → if active and `predictedArrivalEpochMs` in the future and `!alarm_fired`, **re-arm `setAlarmClock` immediately** → restore fired-state latches → attempt live tracking only where FGS-legal (next unlock / foreground), otherwise let the backstop carry it. `completeEndTracking`, the End-Tracking poll path (`alarm_controller.dart:1366`), and `stopTracking` all `cancelBackstop()`.

### Prioritized order

P0 backstop (manifest perms + `ExactAlarmScheduler.kt` + fill `AlarmReceiver.kt` + `exact_alarm_backstop.dart` + snapshot `predictedArrivalEpochMs`) → P1 app `WakeBootReceiver` re-arming the backstop → P2 persist fired-state + snapshot schemaVersion → P3 explicit `autoStartOnBoot`, WorkManager health-worker, battery-opt exemption + OEM onboarding → P4 iOS region-monitoring backstop.

### Adversarial residual gaps (cannot be closed by any API)

- **Force-stop / aggressive OEM kill (the dominant India risk).** A force-stopped app has its AlarmManager alarms **cancelled** and its receivers (incl. `BOOT_COMPLETED`) **disabled** until the user manually relaunches. Both the backstop and boot receiver die. Xiaomi HyperOS/MIUI, Realme/Oppo/Vivo ColorOS, Samsung, and Huawei PowerGenie all do this. Mitigation is onboarding-only: battery-optimization exemption + OEM auto-start/protected-app allowlisting ([dontkillmyapp.com](https://dontkillmyapp.com)). Not programmatically guaranteeable.
- **Huawei without GMS.** `setAlarmClock` is AOSP so the backstop still works, but boot/watchdog need the app on Huawei's protected list.
- **Pre-unlock reboot.** Credential-encrypted SharedPreferences are unavailable until first unlock, so the backstop can't be re-armed until the rider unlocks once (unless device-encrypted storage is added).
- **iOS.** App suspension + force-quit mean only `CLCircularRegion` monitoring / coarse local notifications can wake a suspended app; no exact-time guarantee.

### Build blocker (aside, outside this area)

`android/app` contains **both** `build.gradle` and `build.gradle.kts`; Gradle errors when both exist for one module. Remove one (keep `.kts`; note `targetSdk` is 34 in the legacy `.gradle`) before any of the above compiles.

## WakePoint Reliability Architecture — Single Synthesized Plan

### The one insight that unifies all five inputs
Every failure mode collapses to the same root cause: **the wake guarantee lives inside one Flutter isolate**, on a deliberately silent notification channel, driven per-GPS-tick. Kill/throttle/reboot that isolate and the phone goes silent. The fix is not five separate features — it is **moving the guarantee into the OS and wrapping it in layers that degrade independently.**

### Layers of defense (most-independent-of-a-live-process wins)
| Layer | Mechanism | Survives isolate death? | Survives reboot? | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 — Onboarding | Battery-opt exemption + OEM autostart deep-link + re-nag | enables the rest | — | build |
| 1 — Suspenders | Live EKF/ETA loop fires precise alarm | No | No | exists, harden |
| 2 — **Belt** | `AlarmManager.setAlarmClock` → native `AlarmReceiver` → **self-sounding** FSI channel | **Yes** | needs L4 | **build (core)** |
| 3 — Relaunch backstop | Geofence/region near stop (primary on iOS) | Yes | Yes | build |
| 4 — Boot recovery | Persist target epoch + `BootReceiver` re-arm | Yes | **Yes** | build |

The belt (L2) is the product's actual guarantee: its **sound is baked into the notification channel (USAGE_ALARM)**, so no Dart, no `AlarmPlayer`, no live isolate is needed to make noise. It is armed early by a **60–90s safetyLead** because *late is the only fatal direction*.

### Conflicts between the inputs — resolved
1. **"No wakelock" premise is half-wrong.** `flutter_background_service_android` already holds a `PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK`, so on Android the CPU does **not** suspend while the FGS runs — the real problems are **IMU rate (5 Hz, needs 50 Hz)** and **OEM kill**, not CPU suspend. Do not add a redundant wakelock; just declare `WAKE_LOCK` and win the OEM-exemption fight.
2. **OEM-onboarding vs OS-alarm is not either/or.** ~10–20% of aggressive-OEM users never complete setup or get silently overridden (Samsung OTA re-sleep). The OS belt is the **net** for exactly those users. Build both.
3. **iOS inverts the model.** iOS cannot keep the EKF alive through a tunnel (no background CoreMotion). Its "belt" is **AlarmKit fixed-time alarms (iOS 26+)** driven by the last good ETA — *spatial trigger converted to temporal*. Ship iOS as a **fast-follow**, Android-first.
4. **Reject two tempting hacks:** Critical Alerts entitlement (hand-vetted, likely denied for an indie) and silent-audio keep-alive (Guideline 2.5.4 reject). Neither is a dependency.

### PRIORITIZED BUILD ORDER — biggest reliability gain per unit effort

**MUST-BUILD BEFORE LAUNCH (Android):**
1. **Manifest foundation** (~30 min) — `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS`, `USE_EXACT_ALARM`, `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`, `WAKE_LOCK`; register `.AlarmReceiver` + `.BootReceiver`; OEM-packages `<queries>` block (current one only has `PROCESS_TEXT`). *Native package is `com.example.geowake2`.*
2. **Self-sounding channel + real `AlarmReceiver.kt`** (~1 day) — closes the fatal gap the instant the isolate is dozed or dead. This one step alone is the highest-leverage fix in the codebase.
3. **`geowake/backstop` MethodChannel + `backstop_alarm.dart` + hard-floor arm at `startTracking`** (~1 day) — an OS alarm exists from t0.
4. **Per-tick recompute + cancel-on-fire** in `trackingservice.dart`/`alarm_controller.dart` (~1 day) — precision, no double-fire. `backstopEpoch = now + (etaToDestination − thresholdLead − safetyLead)`, re-arm only if moved >20s.

6. **`BootReceiver.kt`** (~1 day) — re-arm after mid-trip reboot; fire immediately if already past.
7. **Stop the app killing itself** (~0.5 day) — `heartbeat_monitor.dart` must not pause tracking on UI death during a journey; wire `onGpsUnavailable` into production; raise IMU to 50 Hz (`SensorInterval.gameInterval`).

**HARDENING (post-launch / parallel):**
8. FSI permission UX + Play Console declarations + in-app disclosure of un-closable gaps.
9. Measure real background IMU rate on a physical aggressive-OEM device before trusting DR; add non-IMU (time-based) fallback; add the isolate-kill integration test.
10. **iOS fast-follow** — `UIBackgroundModes:[location]` + `AppleSettings` factory across the 3 call-sites + AlarmKit MethodChannel (iOS 26) + geofence/SLC + Time-Sensitive fallback. `NSMotionUsageDescription` is already present.

### Honest end-to-end reliability (rider woken before their stop, 2h, screen-off, backgrounded, with a tunnel), AFTER this architecture

- **(a) Pixel / near-AOSP (Motorola, Nothing):** ~**98–99%**. Battery-opt exemption defeats stock Doze; `setAlarmClock` is the most Doze-resistant primitive; belt + boot recovery cover process death/reboot. Residual: strict user DND, manual Force Stop, extreme battery saver.
- **(b) Xiaomi / aggressive OEM (Redmi, Vivo, Oppo, Realme, OnePlus, Samsung):** ~**90–95% IF the user completes Reliability Setup**, dropping to ~**80–88%** blended because ~10–20% won't complete it or get silently re-restricted (Samsung OTA re-sleep). The OS belt is what holds this above the ~60% floor the current code would deliver. **Huawei no-GMS is effectively unsupported (~50%)** — flag it.
- **(c) iPhone (iOS 26+):** ~**90–93%** — AlarmKit fixed-time alarm fires through suspension/Sleep Focus/silent mode; accuracy bounded by ETA quality on the final tunnel segment, protected by the early safetyLead. **iOS < 26: ~75–85%** on the dismissible Time-Sensitive fallback. iOS genuinely cannot match Android's live tunnel dead-reckoning — it trades spatial-live for temporal-scheduled.

### Bottom line
The layered plan is the right shape and its read of the repo is accurate. But as written it **guarantees the wrong thing**: it makes the belt survive *process death* while leaving it free to fire at a *stale (late) time*, silences it under the *DND state sleeping users have on*, and lets a *recents-swipe* delete it. Fix the belt to be fastest-case (early-biased) + geofence-co-primary, request DND policy access, debounce iOS re-arm, and disclose the un-closable tier (Huawei-no-GMS, Total-Silence DND, thermal-off, force-stop).
